title: CODEX Acquisition Protocol
author: Franchesca Farris
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdifi4bn
materials: Select the Experiment Tab to start the run.
Select Maintenance Wash from the Maintenance tab.
Open the microscope viewer software and login with lab designated PassWord.
Switch back to the CODEX wizard software, select Microscope Pre-Check. Once it passes assessment, Start the run
Close the microscope software and power off the microscope.

steps.title: Remove lid and old coverslip
steps.instruction: Detach the fluidic lid and, if needed, replace the previous coverslip.

substeps.instruction: Untwist the two wing knobs on the coverslip stage to remove the lid holding the fluidic line.
If running two experiments back‑to‑back, remove the old coverslip with bent‑angle forceps, rinse the area well with deionized water, and wipe dry with a kimwipe.

steps.title: Soak gaskets in buffer
steps.instruction: Soak two gaskets in 1 X CODEX buffer for at least ten minutes.

steps.title: Assemble stage insert with coverslip
steps.instruction: Place gaskets and a coverslip into the stage insert, ensuring proper orientation and adhesion.

substeps.instruction: Place the first gasket into the divots at the centre of the stage and tap gently with forceps to seat it.
Place a clean coverslip (or a sample coverslip, tissue side up) on top of the first gasket; tap the edges to ensure adhesion.
Quickly place the second gasket on top of the coverslip.

steps.title: Power on computer and robot
steps.instruction: Turn on the CIM computer and the CODEX robot.

steps.title: Secure stage insert
steps.instruction: Verify correct placement of gaskets and coverslip, then lock the stage insert.

substeps.instruction: Check that the gaskets and coverslip are inserted squarely into the stage.
Place the metal top plate on the stage insert and lock it by turning the wing knobs.
Place the loaded stage insert into the dedicated holder to keep it level during priming.

steps.title: Launch start‑up wizard
steps.instruction: Open the CODEX instrument start‑up Wizard.

steps.title: Create experimental template
steps.instruction: Define all experimental parameters and save the template.

substeps.instruction: Select “New Template” (or “Open Template” to modify an existing one).
Input the Project and Experiment name using the format src_CX_####.
Input the Start Cycle Well and Number of Cycles to match the 96‑well reporter plate.
In the cycle table, enter Marker Name, Exposure time, and Class for each cycle; label the first and last cycles “BLANK” and any unused wells “EMPTY”.
Select the number of Z‑planes (e.g., 11 for a 5 µm section; increase for uneven, large, or thicker sections). The software will adjust the number based on its internal formula.
Click “Validate Experiment” to confirm there are no design errors.
Press “Save Template” or “Save Template As” to store the settings.
Press “Start Experiment”.

steps.title: Follow initial wizard prompts
steps.instruction: Proceed through the start‑up wizard to prime the instrument.

substeps.instruction: Press “Next” on the initial pop‑up describing the wizard steps.
After loading a blank coverslip, click “Next” to continue.
When prompted, click “Prime Instrument” to start priming.

steps.title: Prepare DAPI nuclear stain
steps.instruction: Make fresh DAPI nuclear stain solution.

substeps.instruction: Remove DAPI Nuclear Staining stock solution from 4 °C storage and place it on ice.
Label a 1.5 mL amber microfuge tube for Nuclear Stain Solution.
Add 1 mL of 1 X CODEX Buffer and 0.5 µL DAPI to the tube; invert to mix.

steps.title: Apply nuclear stain to sample
steps.instruction: Load the sample coverslip and add nuclear stain without drying the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Remove the blank coverslip and load the sample coverslip into the stage insert as described in step 3.
Quickly add 700 µL of the Nuclear Stain Solution to the sample well; protect from light.
Ensure the sample coverslip is face up; avoid pipetting directly on the tissue.
If the tissue begins to dry, use a moist kimwipe to clean the underside of the coverslip, then dry the coverslip thoroughly.

steps.title: Incubate and wash tissue
steps.instruction: Allow stain incubation then wash the sample.

substeps.instruction: Press “Wait & Wash Tissue”; the instrument will incubate for five minutes before washing.
If the five‑minute incubation has already passed, click “Immediately Wash Tissue” to remove the nuclear stain solution.

steps.title: Post‑run wash
steps.instruction: Perform a post‑run wash immediately after each CODEX run (≈5 minutes).

steps.title: Clean instrument after run
steps.instruction: Run the clean‑instrument procedure and shut down the system.

substeps.instruction: Remove the stage insert from the microscope and place it in the dedicated holder.
Verify the water bottle contains at least 20 mL of distilled water.
Run “Clean Instrument Wash” from the Maintenance tab.
When the wash finishes, remove the 96‑well plate, empty and clean all reservoirs and bottles.
Close the driver software and turn off the CODEX instrument (note: DMSO is present in all reservoirs and the waste bottle; dispose of liquids properly).

steps.title: Perform routine maintenance wash
steps.instruction: Execute weekly (or monthly) maintenance washing with a blank coverslip.

substeps.instruction: Place a blank coverslip in the stage insert.
Insert caps from Bottle 1 and Bottle 2 into the water bottle to ensure full line cleaning.
Run the Maintenance Wash.
When completed, return fluid lines to their respective bottles, discard the coverslip, wash the gaskets and stage insert with distilled water, and store them dry covered with a kimwipe.

steps.title: Finalize fluidics and power down
steps.instruction: Check fluidics, empty waste, and refill reservoirs before powering off.

substeps.instruction: Click “Check Fluidics”.
Empty the waste bottle, turn off the robot, close the CODEX driver software, and power off the CIM computer.
Fill the water bottle with at least 100 mL distilled water.
Fill Bottle 2 with DMSO and Bottle 1 with 1 X CODEX buffer according to the set‑up chart; reconnect all lines and firmly tighten caps.

steps.title: Set imaging parameters
steps.instruction: Define Z‑plane range, pitch, and stitch area for acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Set the Z‑plane minimum and maximum values; the CIM driver will determine exact planes per tile via autofocus.
Confirm the pitch is set to 1.5 and define a stitch area (e.g., 9 × 9).
Set Z‑planes so the best focus is at the middle of the Z‑stack; verify depth across multiple areas of the sample.

steps.title: Create data storage folder
steps.instruction: Make a folder for raw images and name it with the experimental identifier.

substeps.instruction: Create a folder in the lab share drive “CODEX Runs”.
Name the folder using the experimental name entered in step 7.

steps.title: Prepare microscope and settings
steps.instruction: Power on the microscope and confirm all acquisition settings.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the power supply to the BZ‑X800 Keyence microscope and then turn on the microscope.

Confirm saved settings are compatible with CODEX software: Stage holder = versatile Multichannel ON; all four channels set to white, High resolution, low photobleaching, Monochromatic, Stitching ON, Z‑stacking ON; capture area 7 × 9, pitch 1.5, number of Z‑planes as calculated in step 7.
Remove the 10× and 40× objectives; position the 20× objective for use.
Place the liquid overflow detector in the objective turret with the cord trailing from the left‑side stage cut‑out.
Confirm fluorescent filter cubes are placed as follows: DAPI in position 1, AF750 in position 2, ATTO550 in position 3, Cy5 in position 4.

steps.title: Load stage insert and autofocus
steps.instruction: Insert the stage and focus on the tissue using the DAPI channel.

substeps.instruction: Check that the waste bottle and the four buffer reservoirs inside the instrument are empty and clean.
Place the stage insert into the microscope stage holder.
Activate the DAPI channel and run autofocus on the centre of the tissue sample.

steps.title: Acquire images and save
steps.instruction: Select imaging regions, capture the stitched area, and store the data.

substeps.instruction: Use the Navigation function to select imaging region(s).
Capture an image of the stitch area and save it to the folder created in step 17; confirm the image is routed to the correct folder.
Leave the microscope window open and fully visible; otherwise the driver software may shut down.

steps.title: Verify run completion
steps.instruction: Check the error log to ensure the acquisition finished without issues.
